bibl.title: Tonotopic and non-auditory organization of the mouse dorsal inferior colliculus revealed by two-photon imaging

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the functional organization of the dorsal and lateral cortices of the inferior colliculus, about which RELATIVELY LITTLE IS KNOWN
span.quote: The dorsal (DCIC) and lateral cortices (LCIC) of the inferior colliculus are major targets of the auditory and non-auditory cortical areas, suggesting a role in complex multimodal information processing. However, relatively little is known about their functional organization. We utilized in vivo two-photon Ca 2+ imaging in awake mice expressing GCaMP6s in GABAergic or non-GABAergic neurons in the IC to investigate their spatial organization. We found different classes of temporal responses, which we confirmed with simultaneous juxtacellular electrophysiology. Both GABAergic and non-GABAergic neurons showed spatial microheterogeneity in their temporal responses. In contrast, a robust, double rostromedial-caudolateral gradient of frequency tuning was conserved between the two groups, and even among the subclasses. This, together with the existence of a subset of neurons sensitive to spontaneous movements, provides functional evidence for redefining the border between DCIC and LCIC.

span.label: where the border between DCIC and LCIC actually lies, given that THERE IS LITTLE AGREEMENT ON THE PRECISE BORDERS OF THE DIFFERENT NUCLEI and that ITS PARCELLATION HAS BEEN DIFFERENT BASED ON WHETHER CELL MORPHOLOGY, INPUTS, OR PHYSIOLOGICAL PROPERTIES WERE CHOSEN AS THE MAIN CLASSIFIER
span.quote: There is little agreement on the precise borders of the different nuclei of the IC, and its parcellation has been different based on whether cell morphology, inputs, or physiological properties were chosen as the main classifier ( Oliver, 2005 ). Here we used physiological properties as the main criterion to look at the borders between the DCIC, LCIC and CNIC in the dorsal IC.

span.label: a reversal of the frequency gradient, plus a subset of movement-sensitive neurons on one side of it only, which together PROVIDE FUNCTIONAL EVIDENCE FOR REDEFINING THE BORDER BETWEEN DCIC AND LCIC
span.quote: The dorsal (DCIC) and lateral cortices (LCIC) of the inferior colliculus are major targets of the auditory and non-auditory cortical areas, suggesting a role in complex multimodal information processing. However, relatively little is known about their functional organization. We utilized in vivo two-photon Ca 2+ imaging in awake mice expressing GCaMP6s in GABAergic or non-GABAergic neurons in the IC to investigate their spatial organization. We found different classes of temporal responses, which we confirmed with simultaneous juxtacellular electrophysiology. Both GABAergic and non-GABAergic neurons showed spatial microheterogeneity in their temporal responses. In contrast, a robust, double rostromedial-caudolateral gradient of frequency tuning was conserved between the two groups, and even among the subclasses. This, together with the existence of a subset of neurons sensitive to spontaneous movements, provides functional evidence for redefining the border between DCIC and LCIC.

span.label: existence
span.quote: We found that the dorsal IC is tonotopically organized, with isofrequency bands running in a rostrolateral-caudomedial orientation with frequency tuning varying along the caudolateral-rostromedial direction.

span.label: tonotopic organization of the dorsal inferior colliculus
span.quote: We investigated the functional organization of the dorsal IC in awake mice at the single neuron level.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: We found different classes of temporal responses, which we confirmed with simultaneous juxtacellular electrophysiology.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Extramodular neurons send dendrites into the GAD67-dense neurochemical modules, so that they can sample the somatosensory and motor inputs that terminate there while their somata sit in the auditory extramodular zone
span.quote: We obtained anecdotal evidence that neurons at the border of the modules can extend dendrites into the modules ( Figure 10A,F ), which would allow them to sample non-auditory inputs.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: V-shaped isofrequency axon-terminal plexuses, extended to the dorsal surface, produce the observed reversal of the tonotopic gradient
span.quote: These V-shaped axon terminal plexuses, if extended to the dorsal surface of the IC, provide an anatomical explanation for the observed tonotopic reversal.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Recording in awake rather than anaesthetised animals increases the impact of synaptic inhibition, which generates the unusually frequent offset responses as rebound from inhibition
span.quote: Similar to the inhibition class, we therefore suggest that the prominence of offset responses may be related to the increased impact of synaptic inhibition in the IC of awake animals.

span.label: the border is drawn by a REVERSAL rather than by a feature: A CENTRAL STRIP RUNNING IN THE CAUDOMEDIAL-ROSTROLATERAL ORIENTATION OF CELLS RESPONDING TO LOWER FREQUENCIES, WHILE CF PROGRESSIVELY INCREASED IN BOTH THE CAUDOLATERAL AND THE ROSTROMEDIAL DIRECTION
span.quote: Interestingly, we observed a central strip running in the caudomedial-rostrolateral orientation of cells responding to lower frequencies, while CF progressively increased in both the caudolateral and the rostromedial direction.

span.label: THE LATEROCAUDAL AREA WITH HIGH FREQUENCIES IS THE DORSAL EDGE OF THE LCIC, WHEREAS THE MEDIOROSTRAL PART OF THE DORSAL IC BELONGS TO THE DCIC, so THE TONOTOPIC REVERSAL WOULD THUS PROVIDE A FUNCTIONAL DEMARCATION BETWEEN THE DORSAL AND LATERAL CORTICES OF THE IC
span.quote: Our findings suggest that the laterocaudal area with high frequencies is the dorsal edge of the LCIC, whereas the mediorostral part of the dorsal IC belongs to the DCIC. The tonotopic reversal would thus provide a functional demarcation between the dorsal and lateral cortices of the IC.

span.label: the proposed route by which a cell outside a module can receive the module's input - NEURONS AT THE BORDER OF THE MODULES CAN EXTEND DENDRITES INTO THE MODULES, WHICH WOULD ALLOW THEM TO SAMPLE NON-AUDITORY INPUTS - offered as ANECDOTAL EVIDENCE
span.quote: We obtained anecdotal evidence that neurons at the border of the modules can extend dendrites into the modules ( Figure 10A,F ), which would allow them to sample non-auditory inputs.

span.label: THESE V-SHAPED AXON TERMINAL PLEXUSES, IF EXTENDED TO THE DORSAL SURFACE OF THE IC, PROVIDE AN ANATOMICAL EXPLANATION FOR THE OBSERVED TONOTOPIC REVERSAL
span.quote: These V-shaped axon terminal plexuses, if extended to the dorsal surface of the IC, provide an anatomical explanation for the observed tonotopic reversal.

span.label: The GAD67-dense modules on the medial side of the IC could not be imaged, so their relation to somatosensory input is unresolved.
span.quote: The medial modules could not be imaged within this study, so their association with somatosensory inputs is currently unclear.

span.label: Different kinds of spontaneous movement were not separated because they co-occurred.
span.quote: We did not further discriminate between different movements as they tended to be heavily correlated.

span.label: The rostromedial arm of the frequency gradient rests on few sampled neurons.
span.quote: The increase in CFs on the rostromedial side was not as pronounced, likely due to the low number of neurons sampled in this region.

span.label: Correlating spontaneous activity with movement cannot establish which non-auditory input drives the movement-related responses.
span.quote: Direct stimulation of the different non-auditory inputs would be needed to obtain a better idea of their importance for the observed facial or body movement-related responses.

span.label: the fit that carries the organisational claim EXPLAINED AROUND 13% OF THE VARIANCE IN CFs
span.quote: The solid line in Figure 6B shows the best polynomial fit, which explained around 13% of the variance in CFs.

span.label: THERE WAS AN OVER-REPRESENTATION OF LOW CF NEURONS IN THE DEEPEST REGIONS, which the authors ATTRIBUTE TO A SAMPLING BIAS IN WHICH THE LOW FREQUENCY REGION COINCIDED WITH THE CENTER OF THE CRANIAL WINDOW, WHERE IT WAS POSSIBLE TO IMAGE SOMEWHAT DEEPER THAN TOWARDS THE EDGES
span.quote: There was an over-representation of low CF neurons in the deepest regions (121–160 μm deep, Figure 6E,F ). We attribute this to a sampling bias in which the low frequency region coincided with the center of the cranial window, where it was possible to image somewhat deeper than towards the edges

span.label: the identity of the structure imaged is not certain - WE DO NOT EXCLUDE THE POSSIBILITY OF IMAGING INTO THE CENTRAL NUCLEUS OF THE IC
span.quote: While we do not exclude the possibility of imaging into the central nucleus of the IC, we believe the observed tonotopy to be a good representation of the IC shell region because all CFs were represented among the most superficial neurons

span.label: WE FOUND CONSIDERABLE VARIABILITY IN CFs WITHIN A BAND, and SUBSTANTIAL VARIABILITY WAS ALSO OBSERVED WITHIN A SINGLE ANIMAL, so alignment error between animals is not the whole of it
span.quote: We found considerable variability in CFs within a band. Imprecisions in the alignment of imaging areas and variability between animals may have contributed to the variability, but substantial variability was also observed within a single animal, in line with previous results

span.label: A SUBSTANTIAL FRACTION OF CELLS DID NOT RESPOND TO TONES, and three reasons are offered without deciding between them - LOW PROBABILITY RESPONSES MAY HAVE BEEN BELOW DETECTION, SOME CELLS MAY RESPOND PREFERENTIALLY TO MORE COMPLEX SOUND STIMULI, and SOME CELLS MAY PREFER SOMATOSENSORY OR MOTOR STIMULI INSTEAD OF SOUND STIMULI
span.quote: A substantial fraction of cells did not respond to tones. Low probability responses may have been below detection, since the juxtacellular recordings indicated that single APs could not always be detected. Some cells may respond preferentially to more complex sound stimuli, as previously found for neurons in the shell region ( Ehret and Moffat, 1985 ; Aitkin et al., 1994 ). As discussed below, some cells may prefer somatosensory or motor stimuli instead of sound stimuli.

span.label: the one response class that carries part of the argument has no ground truth - DUE TO THEIR RARITY, WE HAVE NOT OBTAINED A SIMULTANEOUS RECORDING FOR OFFSET CELLS
span.quote: Due to their rarity, we have not obtained a simultaneous recording for offset cells.

span.label: the selection criteria are blind to the effect the literature expects - FOR SOMATOSENSORY INPUTS, THE DOMINANT EFFECT APPEARS TO BE INHIBITORY, and ONLY A MINORITY OF CELLS HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO RESPOND TO UNIMODAL TACTILE STIMULI, WHICH WOULD NOT HELP DETECTION BASED ON OUR SELECTION CRITERIA
span.quote: For somatosensory inputs, the dominant effect appears to be inhibitory and only a minority of cells have been shown to respond to unimodal tactile stimuli ( Aitkin et al., 1978 ; Aitkin et al., 1981 ; Zhou and Shore, 2006 ), which would not help detection based on our selection criteria.

span.label: the labeling is one-way: VIRTUALLY ALL NEURONS EXPRESSING GCaMP6s IN THE GP4.3 LINE WERE GLUTAMATERGIC, BUT NOT ALL GLUTAMATERGIC NEURONS WERE LABELED, and A SYSTEMATIC SCREEN OF MARKERS WOULD BE NEEDED TO TEST FOR A SELECTIVE ENRICHMENT OF GLUTAMATERGIC SUBTYPES IN THE GP4.3 LINE
span.quote: We confirmed that virtually all neurons expressing GCaMP6s in the GP4.3 line were glutamatergic, but not all glutamatergic neurons were labeled. There may have been a preponderance of labeled cells around the modules in the LCIC ( Figure 1D ), but a systematic screen of markers would be needed to test for a selective enrichment of glutamatergic subtypes in the GP4.3 line.

span.label: DIRECT STIMULATION OF THE DIFFERENT NON-AUDITORY INPUTS WOULD BE NEEDED TO OBTAIN A BETTER IDEA OF THEIR IMPORTANCE FOR THE OBSERVED FACIAL OR BODY MOVEMENT-RELATED RESPONSES
span.quote: Direct stimulation of the different non-auditory inputs would be needed to obtain a better idea of their importance for the observed facial or body movement-related responses.

span.label: WE DID NOT FURTHER DISCRIMINATE BETWEEN DIFFERENT MOVEMENTS AS THEY TENDED TO BE HEAVILY CORRELATED
span.quote: We monitored spontaneous whisker and general body movements, and used strict criteria to exclude movement artefacts. As we restricted the analysis to neurons that were not excited by tones, we consider it unlikely that the observed movement-related responses were caused by self-generated sounds. Despite these severe restrictions, we did find that a few percent of the cells were excited during whisker or body movements, suggesting a substantial role for somatosensory or motor inputs.

span.label: the banding pattern used as independent support for the reversal - THIS REVERSAL IS IN LINE WITH THE BANDING PATTERNS OBSERVED WITH EPIFLUORESCENT CALCIUM IMAGING IN UNANESTHETIZED MICE BEFORE AND AT HEARING ONSET
span.quote: Interestingly, our data are also compatible with two earlier two-photon calcium imaging studies ( Ito et al., 2014 ; Barnstedt et al., 2015 ). Ito et al. (2014) reported gradients in the medial regions of the dorsal IC, which ran from lateral (low-frequency) to medial (high-frequency), whereas Barnstedt et al. (2015) reported gradients in a mediorostral to laterocaudal direction.

span.label: cells whose transients lacked the indicator's own decay kinetics thrown out
span.quote: By correlating movement and fluorescence, we detected 165 (out of 1359) cells that showed a positive correlation ( r > 0.25) with facial movements during the spontaneous recording period. To exclude potential false-positive detection due to motion artefacts (i.e. cells moving into and out of focus), we excluded cells with fluorescence transients that did not show the typical ~1 s exponential decay kinetics, which last much longer than the brief image shifts that could accompany movement events (image shifts in Figure 8A , Figure 8—figure supplement 1 ). Since animal movement inevitably produces sound that may activate the IC neurons, leading to an apparent movement sensitivity, we also excluded the cells that showed excitatory or offset responses in their FRA. In the end, 41 cells showed spontaneous calcium transients that correlated with animal movement and that could not be explained by their FRA, which was either inhibited-type or showed no clear pure tone evoked responses

span.label: every cell with an excitatory or offset tone response removed from the movement analysis
span.quote: By correlating movement and fluorescence, we detected 165 (out of 1359) cells that showed a positive correlation ( r > 0.25) with facial movements during the spontaneous recording period. To exclude potential false-positive detection due to motion artefacts (i.e. cells moving into and out of focus), we excluded cells with fluorescence transients that did not show the typical ~1 s exponential decay kinetics, which last much longer than the brief image shifts that could accompany movement events (image shifts in Figure 8A , Figure 8—figure supplement 1 ). Since animal movement inevitably produces sound that may activate the IC neurons, leading to an apparent movement sensitivity, we also excluded the cells that showed excitatory or offset responses in their FRA. In the end, 41 cells showed spontaneous calcium transients that correlated with animal movement and that could not be explained by their FRA, which was either inhibited-type or showed no clear pure tone evoked responses

span.label: the tonotopic fit re-run on cells within 50 micrometers of the surface only
span.quote: Based on a clustering analysis, Barnstedt et al. (2015) suggested that the central strip of low frequency neurons were from the most dorsal end of the central nucleus, and we did observe a small but significant correlation between depth and log(CF) ( Figure 6—figure supplement 7 ; correlation coefficient = −0.22; n = 799; p=3 × 10 −10 ). However, a plot of CF along the best orientation from the polynomial fit as a function of depth illustrates that most cells were located within 100 µm from the surface, and that the low frequency neurons were also among the most superficial cells

span.label: the depth-CF correlation re-computed inside the central strip alone
span.quote: Based on a clustering analysis, Barnstedt et al. (2015) suggested that the central strip of low frequency neurons were from the most dorsal end of the central nucleus, and we did observe a small but significant correlation between depth and log(CF) ( Figure 6—figure supplement 7 ; correlation coefficient = −0.22; n = 799; p=3 × 10 −10 ). However, a plot of CF along the best orientation from the polynomial fit as a function of depth illustrates that most cells were located within 100 µm from the surface, and that the low frequency neurons were also among the most superficial cells

span.label: the fluorescence classes checked against spikes in the same cell, by simultaneous juxtacellular recording in awake animals
span.quote: To relate the different fluorescence responses to spiking patterns, which are highly heterogeneous within the IC (e.g. Willott et al., 1988a ; Willott et al., 1988b ; Tan and Borst, 2007 ), we combined Ca 2+ imaging with in vivo juxtacellular recordings in awake mice. We recorded from neurons showing onset, sustained and inhibitory tone-evoked fluorescence responses. For fluorescence responses that we classified as onset, electrophysiological recordings showed that this class can represent a cell whose firing rate quickly adapted during our one-second long stimuli (example in Figure 5A–C,D left). We observed sustained fluorescence responses that corresponded to sustained firing ( Figure 5D middle) with different amount of adaptation. Inhibitory responses corresponded to cells that reduced their spontaneous firing upon sound stimulation

span.label: the polynomial order raised until it stopped helping
span.quote: We used a polynomial model fit as a way to extract any general direction along which CFs may diverge, without imposing any presumption about the spatial CF dependence. We found that a fourth order polynomial captured the variance maximally; further increasing its order did not lead to better fits.

span.label: the transgenic labels checked against GAD67 immunolabeling
span.quote: The large majority (4651/4898; 95%) of GCaMP-positive neurons in the GP4.3 line were not positive for GAD67 ( Figure 1A–D ), showing that the Thy1-promoter preferentially expressed GCaMP6s in non-GABAergic cells in the IC

span.label: THE BORDER DEPENDS ON WHICH CLASSIFIER YOU PICK, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO BEFORE MOVING IT: THERE IS LITTLE AGREEMENT ON THE PRECISE BORDERS OF THE DIFFERENT NUCLEI OF THE IC, AND ITS PARCELLATION HAS BEEN DIFFERENT BASED ON WHETHER CELL MORPHOLOGY, INPUTS, OR PHYSIOLOGICAL PROPERTIES WERE CHOSEN AS THE MAIN CLASSIFIER - HERE WE USED PHYSIOLOGICAL PROPERTIES AS THE MAIN CRITERION
span.quote: There is little agreement on the precise borders of the different nuclei of the IC, and its parcellation has been different based on whether cell morphology, inputs, or physiological properties were chosen as the main classifier ( Oliver, 2005 ). Here we used physiological properties as the main criterion to look at the borders between the DCIC, LCIC and CNIC in the dorsal IC.

span.label: AND TWO PUBLISHED ATLASES DRAW THE SAME DEMARCATION AT NINETY DEGREES TO EACH OTHER: THE MINIMUM FREQUENCY LINE ALIGNS WITH THE DEMARCATION FROM THE ALLEN REFERENCE ATLAS, WHILE THAT BY PAXINOS AND FRANKLIN LAYS IN THE ORTHOGONAL DIRECTION. Both are in current use; a coordinate tagged to one of them is not tagged to the other
span.quote: We overlaid the line representing the neurons with the lowest CF and compared its location with the border of LCIC and DCIC traced from the latest Allen Reference Atlas (CCFv3) and from the classical reference atlas by Paxinos and Franklin (2001) . The minimum frequency line aligns with the demarcation from the Allen Reference Atlas, while that by Paxinos and Franklin lays in the orthogonal direction.

span.label: THE FEATURE THAT DEFINES ONE SIDE IS FOUND ON BOTH SIDES: SURPRISINGLY, WE OBSERVED GAD67-DENSE MODULES IN BOTH THE MEDIAL AND THE LATERAL ASPECT OF THE IC, THAT IS WITHIN BOTH LCIC AND DCIC IN EITHER ATLAS - and the modules are A DEFINING FEATURE OF THE LCIC
span.quote: Surprisingly, we observed GAD67-dense modules in both the medial and the lateral aspect of the IC (arrowheads Figure 9A,G ), that is within both LCIC and DCIC in either atlas.

span.label: the claim the title rests on is a direction, not a location: THE SOLID LINE SHOWS THE BEST POLYNOMIAL FIT, WHICH EXPLAINED AROUND 13% OF THE VARIANCE IN CFs. The organisation is real and it predicts almost nothing about any individual cell
span.quote: The solid line in Figure 6B shows the best polynomial fit, which explained around 13% of the variance in CFs.

span.label: and the paper says the variability is not measurement error: WE FOUND CONSIDERABLE VARIABILITY IN CFs WITHIN A BAND, and SUBSTANTIAL VARIABILITY WAS ALSO OBSERVED WITHIN A SINGLE ANIMAL
span.quote: We found considerable variability in CFs within a band. Imprecisions in the alignment of imaging areas and variability between animals may have contributed to the variability, but substantial variability was also observed within a single animal, in line with previous results

span.label: A SAMPLING BIAS NAMED WITH ITS PHYSICAL CAUSE: THERE WAS AN OVER-REPRESENTATION OF LOW CF NEURONS IN THE DEEPEST REGIONS, attributed to THE LOW FREQUENCY REGION COINCIDING WITH THE CENTER OF THE CRANIAL WINDOW, WHERE IT WAS POSSIBLE TO IMAGE SOMEWHAT DEEPER THAN TOWARDS THE EDGES - the optics of the window, not the tissue
span.quote: There was an over-representation of low CF neurons in the deepest regions (121–160 μm deep, Figure 6E,F ). We attribute this to a sampling bias in which the low frequency region coincided with the center of the cranial window, where it was possible to image somewhat deeper than towards the edges

span.label: THE IDENTITY OF WHAT WAS MEASURED IS LEFT OPEN: WHILE WE DO NOT EXCLUDE THE POSSIBILITY OF IMAGING INTO THE CENTRAL NUCLEUS OF THE IC, WE BELIEVE THE OBSERVED TONOTOPY TO BE A GOOD REPRESENTATION OF THE IC SHELL REGION
span.quote: While we do not exclude the possibility of imaging into the central nucleus of the IC, we believe the observed tonotopy to be a good representation of the IC shell region because all CFs were represented among the most superficial neurons

span.label: TWO CLASSES OF RESPONSE EXIST BECAUSE THE ANIMAL WAS AWAKE AND THE TONE WAS LONG: INHIBITORY AND OFFSET RESPONSES WERE NOT REPORTED IN EARLIER IMAGING EXPERIMENTS PERFORMED IN ANESTHETIZED MICE, and THEIR USE OF SHORTER STIMULI DID NOT ALLOW A DISTINCTION BETWEEN ONSET AND SUSTAINED RESPONSES. Two conditions, two whole response categories
span.quote: Inhibitory and offset responses were not reported in earlier imaging experiments performed in anesthetized mice ( Ito et al., 2014 ; Barnstedt et al., 2015 ); their use of shorter stimuli did not allow a distinction between onset and sustained responses.

span.label: and the size of that difference is stated against a named earlier number: THE PROPORTION OF CELLS SHOWING SOUND-EVOKED INHIBITION WAS CLEARLY HIGHER THAN THE 2-23% REPORTED FOR ANESTHETIZED C57BL/6 MICE
span.quote: The proportion of cells showing sound-evoked inhibition was clearly higher than the 2–23% reported for anesthetized C57BL/6 mice in Willott et al. (1988a)

span.label: OFFSET RESPONSES ARE GENERALLY RESTRICTED TO CELLS SHOWING BAND-PASS DURATION TUNING, WHICH ONLY RESPONDED TO MUCH SHORTER TONES THAN THE 1 S EMPLOYED HERE - so finding them at all is the finding
span.quote: However, studies in the IC of anesthetized mice, rats and chinchillas showed that offset responses are generally restricted to cells showing band-pass duration tuning, which only responded to much shorter tones than the 1 s employed here ( Chen, 1998 ; Brand et al., 2000 ; Pérez-González et al., 2006 ). Another striking finding was therefore that we saw clear evidence for offset responses in 3–11% of sound-responsive cells.

span.label: TWO EARLIER PAPERS REPORTED GRADIENTS IN DIFFERENT DIRECTIONS AND THIS ONE IS COMPATIBLE WITH BOTH: ITO ET AL. REPORTED GRADIENTS RUNNING FROM LATERAL (LOW-FREQUENCY) TO MEDIAL (HIGH-FREQUENCY), WHEREAS BARNSTEDT ET AL. REPORTED GRADIENTS IN A MEDIOROSTRAL TO LATEROCAUDAL DIRECTION - a reversal makes two opposite gradients the same finding, seen from two sides of the minimum
span.quote: Interestingly, our data are also compatible with two earlier two-photon calcium imaging studies ( Ito et al., 2014 ; Barnstedt et al., 2015 ). Ito et al. (2014) reported gradients in the medial regions of the dorsal IC, which ran from lateral (low-frequency) to medial (high-frequency), whereas Barnstedt et al. (2015) reported gradients in a mediorostral to laterocaudal direction.

span.label: THE SAME MEASUREMENT MADE IN A neighborING STRUCTURE GIVES THE OPPOSITE ANSWER: OUR RESULTS THUS DIFFER FROM AUDITORY CORTEX, WHERE LOCAL MICROHETEROGENEITY IS MUCH SMALLER FOR (PARVALBUMIN-POSITIVE) GABAERGIC NEURONS THAN FOR GLUTAMATERGIC NEURONS, and here THE MICROHETEROGENEITY WAS SIMILAR FOR GABAERGIC AND GLUTAMATERGIC NEURONS
span.quote: Our results thus differ from auditory cortex, where response patterns are different and local microheterogeneity is much smaller for (parvalbumin-positive) GABAergic neurons than for glutamatergic neurons ( Maor et al., 2016 ; Liang et al., 2018 ; Liu et al., 2019 ). We conclude that despite the shared input and firing behavior during development ( Babola et al., 2018 ), functional heterogeneity dominates within bands in the dorsal IC of adult mice.

span.label: and one candidate cause of a disagreement is the indicator, not the tissue: THIS MICROHETEROGENEITY WAS LARGER THAN IN AN EARLIER STUDY IN WHICH BULK LOADING OF AN ORGANIC Ca INDICATOR WAS USED, WHICH MAY HAVE MADE IT MORE DIFFICULT TO ISOLATE RESPONSES FROM INDIVIDUAL CELLS
span.quote: This microheterogeneity was larger than in an earlier study in which bulk loading of an organic Ca indicator was used ( Ito et al., 2014 ), which may have made it more difficult to isolate responses from individual cells.

span.label: THE COUNT THAT SURVIVES TWO EXCLUSIONS IS THE ONE REPORTED: 165 (OUT OF 1359) CELLS SHOWED A POSITIVE CORRELATION WITH FACIAL MOVEMENTS, and IN THE END, 41 CELLS SHOWED SPONTANEOUS CALCIUM TRANSIENTS THAT CORRELATED WITH ANIMAL MOVEMENT AND THAT COULD NOT BE EXPLAINED BY THEIR FRA
span.quote: By correlating movement and fluorescence, we detected 165 (out of 1359) cells that showed a positive correlation ( r > 0.25) with facial movements during the spontaneous recording period. To exclude potential false-positive detection due to motion artefacts (i.e. cells moving into and out of focus), we excluded cells with fluorescence transients that did not show the typical ~1 s exponential decay kinetics, which last much longer than the brief image shifts that could accompany movement events (image shifts in Figure 8A , Figure 8—figure supplement 1 ). Since animal movement inevitably produces sound that may activate the IC neurons, leading to an apparent movement sensitivity, we also excluded the cells that showed excitatory or offset responses in their FRA. In the end, 41 cells showed spontaneous calcium transients that correlated with animal movement and that could not be explained by their FRA, which was either inhibited-type or showed no clear pure tone evoked responses

span.label: A NEGATIVE THAT DOES THE ARGUMENTATIVE WORK: MOVEMENT-SENSITIVE NEURONS WERE NOT FOUND IN THE HIGH-FREQUENCY DCIC REGIONS, BUT ONLY IN THE PUTATIVE CNIC REGION AND THE LCIC. The border is drawn by where the cells are ABSENT
span.quote: Movement-sensitive neurons were not found in the high-frequency DCIC regions, but only in the putative CNIC region and the LCIC.

span.label: and the detection method could not have found the effect the literature predicts: FOR SOMATOSENSORY INPUTS, THE DOMINANT EFFECT APPEARS TO BE INHIBITORY, WHICH WOULD NOT HELP DETECTION BASED ON OUR SELECTION CRITERIA
span.quote: For somatosensory inputs, the dominant effect appears to be inhibitory and only a minority of cells have been shown to respond to unimodal tactile stimuli ( Aitkin et al., 1978 ; Aitkin et al., 1981 ; Zhou and Shore, 2006 ), which would not help detection based on our selection criteria.

span.label: AN EVIDENTIAL STATUS STATED IN THE TEXT: WE OBTAINED ANECDOTAL EVIDENCE THAT NEURONS AT THE BORDER OF THE MODULES CAN EXTEND DENDRITES INTO THE MODULES. The mechanism that answers the paper's own open question is offered as anecdote, in the authors' own word
span.quote: We obtained anecdotal evidence that neurons at the border of the modules can extend dendrites into the modules ( Figure 10A,F ), which would allow them to sample non-auditory inputs.

span.label: and the question it answers is stated as a problem for the field, not for this paper: THESE INPUTS TARGET THE LAYER TWO MODULES, WHICH CONSTITUTE ONLY A SMALL FRACTION OF THE LCIC VOLUME - THIS RAISES THE QUESTION HOW SO MANY CELLS IN THE LCIC CAN BE SENSITIVE TO NON-AUDITORY INPUTS
span.quote: These inputs target the layer two modules, which constitute only a small fraction of the LCIC volume. Moreover, neurons in the modules do not seem to target extramodular IC neurons ( Lesicko and Llano, 2019 ). This raises the question how so many cells in the LCIC can be sensitive to non-auditory inputs.

span.label: THE LABEL IS PURE IN ONE DIRECTION ONLY: 95% OF GCaMP-POSITIVE NEURONS IN THE GP4.3 LINE WERE NOT POSITIVE FOR GAD67, and NOT ALL NON-GABAERGIC CELLS WERE GCaMP-POSITIVE - what the label includes is known, what it misses is not
span.quote: The large majority (4651/4898; 95%) of GCaMP-positive neurons in the GP4.3 line were not positive for GAD67 ( Figure 1A–D ), showing that the Thy1-promoter preferentially expressed GCaMP6s in non-GABAergic cells in the IC

span.label: the same asymmetry in the other line: GAD67 IMMUNOREACTIVITY was detected IN >93% OF GCaMP-POSITIVE NEURONS IN THE Gad2;Ai96 MICE, and NOT ALL GAD67-POSITIVE CELLS IN THIS MOUSE LINE WERE LABELED BY GCaMP6s
span.quote: In contrast, we detected GAD67 immunoreactivity in >93% (1702/1828) of GCaMP-positive neurons in the Gad2;Ai96 mice ( Figure 1D,H–O ). Not all GAD67-positive cells in this mouse line were labeled by GCaMP6s

span.label: A MARKER THAT DOES NOT PLACE A CELL: AT THE SINGLE NEURON LEVEL, THE PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF THE TWO BUFFERS WAS INSUFFICIENT TO INDICATE WHETHER THE NEURONS LAY WITHIN A MODULE
span.quote: At the single neuron level, the presence or absence of the two buffers was insufficient to indicate whether the neurons lay within a module. These results suggest that for both lines there is not a clear enrichment of GCaMP6+ neurons within the neurochemical modules.

span.label: and the conclusion is stated as a definition rather than a discovery: OUR EXPERIMENTS THUS PROVIDE A FUNCTIONAL DEFINITION OF THE MAJOR ORGANIZATION PRINCIPLES OF THE DORSAL IC IN ADULT MICE
span.quote: We investigated the functional organization of the dorsal IC in awake mice at the single neuron level. We found that the dorsal IC is tonotopically organized, with isofrequency bands running in a rostrolateral-caudomedial orientation with frequency tuning varying along the caudolateral-rostromedial direction. The lowest CF band was found in the middle, dividing the dorsal IC into two reversed tonotopic gradients. In the caudolateral part, but not in the rostromedial part, neurons that were sensitive to whisker or other movements were found, which was in agreement with the view that the caudolateral and rostromedial part corresponded to the LCIC and DCIC, respectively. We observed four different types of firing patterns in response to tones, but other than the tonotopical organization, no obvious topographical organization was observed for the firing patterns. GABAergic neurons were on average somewhat larger, but otherwise there were not clear differences with glutamatergic neurons in spatial organization or firing patterns. Our experiments thus provide a functional definition of the major organization principles of the dorsal IC in adult mice.

span.label: 64% (696 out of 1090) — proportion of GP4.3 (non-GABAergic) cells with detectable fluorescence responses to 1 s pure tones
span.quote: In GP4.3 mice, 64% of the cells (696 out of 1090) cells showed detectable fluorescence changes in response to 1 s pure tone stimuli.

span.label: 73% (247 out of 342 cells) — proportion of GABAergic (Gad2;Ai96) cells with consistent fluorescence responses to 1 s pure tones
span.quote: In Gad2;Ai96 mice 73% (247 out of 342 cells) of GCaMP6s-positive IC neurons showed consistent fluorescence responses to 1 s pure tone stimuli.

span.label: 4651/4898; 95% — share of GCaMP-positive cells in the GP4.3 line that were GAD67-negative, i.e. non-GABAergic
span.quote: The large majority (4651/4898; 95%) of GCaMP-positive neurons in the GP4.3 line were not positive for GAD67 ( Figure 1A–D ), showing that the Thy1-promoter preferentially expressed GCaMP6s in non-GABAergic cells in the IC.

span.label: ~44% — share of sound-responsive IC neurons showing inhibitory responses
span.quote: The prominence of inhibitory responses in the IC (~44% of sound-responsive neurons) in both transgenic lines was a striking finding in our recordings.

span.label: 50° — best-fit angle of the tonotopic gradient axis relative to the medial-lateral axis
span.quote: The best fit yielded an angle θ of 50° from the medial-lateral axis.

span.label: around 13% — variance in characteristic frequency explained by the fourth-order polynomial tonotopy fit
span.quote: The solid line in Figure 6B shows the best polynomial fit, which explained around 13% of the variance in CFs.

span.label: 165 (out of 1359) — cells whose fluorescence correlated positively with facial movement before artefact and sound-confound exclusions
span.quote: By correlating movement and fluorescence, we detected 165 (out of 1359) cells that showed a positive correlation

span.label: 41 cells — cells retained as genuinely movement-sensitive after excluding motion artefacts and sound-responsive cells
span.quote: In the end, 41 cells showed spontaneous calcium transients that correlated with animal movement and that could not be explained by their FRA, which was either inhibited-type or showed no clear pure tone evoked responses (example FRAs in Figure 8F ).

span.label: around 13% — the variance in CFs explained by the polynomial fit that defines the tonotopic direction
span.quote: The solid line in Figure 6B shows the best polynomial fit, which explained around 13% of the variance in CFs.

span.label: 41 — cells with movement-correlated transients surviving both exclusions, out of 165 correlated and 1359 recorded
span.quote: By correlating movement and fluorescence, we detected 165 (out of 1359) cells that showed a positive correlation ( r > 0.25) with facial movements during the spontaneous recording period. To exclude potential false-positive detection due to motion artefacts (i.e. cells moving into and out of focus), we excluded cells with fluorescence transients that did not show the typical ~1 s exponential decay kinetics, which last much longer than the brief image shifts that could accompany movement events (image shifts in Figure 8A , Figure 8—figure supplement 1 ). Since animal movement inevitably produces sound that may activate the IC neurons, leading to an apparent movement sensitivity, we also excluded the cells that showed excitatory or offset responses in their FRA. In the end, 41 cells showed spontaneous calcium transients that correlated with animal movement and that could not be explained by their FRA, which was either inhibited-type or showed no clear pure tone evoked responses

span.label: ~44% — of sound-responsive neurons showing inhibitory responses, against 2-23% reported in anesthetized mice
span.quote: The prominence of inhibitory responses in the IC (~44% of sound-responsive neurons) in both transgenic lines was a striking finding in our recordings. An important factor contributing to their prominence is probably that our experiments were done in awake animals, as a recent single unit recording study showed the presence of inhibitory responses as well as higher spontaneous spike rates in IC neurons of awake mice compared to mice under urethane anesthesia ( Duque and Malmierca, 2015 ), and synaptic inhibition has also been shown to be prominently present in whole-cell recordings in awake bats

span.label: 3-11% — of sound-responsive cells showing offset responses, which earlier work restricted to duration-tuned cells
span.quote: However, studies in the IC of anesthetized mice, rats and chinchillas showed that offset responses are generally restricted to cells showing band-pass duration tuning, which only responded to much shorter tones than the 1 s employed here ( Chen, 1998 ; Brand et al., 2000 ; Pérez-González et al., 2006 ). Another striking finding was therefore that we saw clear evidence for offset responses in 3–11% of sound-responsive cells.

span.quote: The large majority (4651/4898; 95%) of GCaMP-positive neurons in the GP4.3 line were not positive for GAD67 ( Figure 1A–D ), showing that the Thy1-promoter preferentially expressed GCaMP6s in non-GABAergic cells in the IC

span.label: 50% and 95% — the range of fluorescence variance the spike-to-fluorescence model explains, median 79%
span.quote: The model could explain between 50% and 95% of the variance in the fluorescence (median: 79%; average ±s.d.: 77 ± 13%).
